title: History Lane
note: Canyon from a trailer of Italian parts to Kona. Dates from Canyon’s own history page, Wikipedia and press coverage; photographs from Wikimedia Commons, painted (tools/paint_canvases.py) and credited. The sculptures are abstract tributes, not likenesses.

canvases.caption: The Canyon store in Koblenz, February 2008 (closed in 2009)
A Speedmax on display in Koblenz, October 2023

chapters.title: A trailer at the races
chapters.text: Roman Arnold's father imported Italian bike parts and sold them from a trailer on the sidelines of his son's races.

chapters.title: Radsport Arnold
chapters.text: Roman Arnold and his brother Franc found Radsport Arnold, a retailer of bike parts, and open their first shop in the city centre of Koblenz.

chapters.title: The first Canyon
chapters.text: The first Canyon-branded bike reaches the market — a mountain bike. No photograph of it is held here; the frame stays empty.

chapters.title: The first Speedmax
chapters.text: Rad Sport Arnold sells the aluminium Speedmax 1000, 2000 and 3000 with a 75° “Triathlon 2000” geometry; TRIATHLET reviews the Speedmax 2000 in its September 1999 issue.

chapters.title: From dealer to maker
chapters.text: The company becomes a bicycle manufacturer and hires frame designer Lutz Scheffer.

chapters.title: The name Canyon
chapters.text: Radsport Arnold is renamed Canyon Bicycles GmbH.

chapters.title: Direct, online
chapters.text: Canyon starts selling bikes to customers online, directly — the model that drives its growth.

chapters.title: A pro team
chapters.text: Canyon equips its first professional team, UCI ProTour squad Unibet.com, including a Speedmax time-trial bike.

chapters.title: The Koblenz store
chapters.text: The Canyon store in Koblenz, photographed in February 2008. It closed in 2009.

chapters.title: Headquarters
chapters.text: Canyon’s headquarters in Koblenz, in a photograph released by the company in 2009.

chapters.title: Speedmax CF
chapters.text: The carbon Speedmax CF, previewed at Eurobike 2011 with “Trident” tube profiles, wins a red dot “best of the best” award.

chapters.title: Kona
chapters.text: Jan Frodeno wins the Ironman World Championship on a Speedmax CF SLX — the first of Canyon’s Kona titles. (Photo: Canyon in Koblenz, July 2015.)

chapters.title: Canyon Home
chapters.text: Canyon Home in Koblenz, photographed in September 2019. That October, Frodeno wins Kona again in a course record.

chapters.title: A new chapter
chapters.text: Roman Arnold steps back as CEO to chair Canyon’s advisory board. In December, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert takes a majority stake; Arnold reinvests alongside it.

chapters.title: Still Koblenz
chapters.text: A Speedmax on display in Koblenz, where it all started. The next year Patrick Lange sets the Kona course record on a Speedmax CFR.
